title: Magnetic field-driven phase switching in the antiferromagnetic Mott insulator Ca$_3$(Ru$_{0.99}$Ti$_{0.01}$)$_2$O$_7$
authors: Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, George Jackeli, Maximilian J. Krautloher, Pascal Reiss, Eberhard J. Goering, Jurgen H. Smet, Bernhard Keimer, Alexander V. Boris
abstract: A bandwidth-controlled antiferromagnetic Mott-insulating phase in Ca$_3$(Ru$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$)$_2$O$_7$ is realized through isovalent substitution at the Ru site. For a dilute substitution with only 1% Ti, the Mott insulator ground state remains nearly degenerate with the ground state of pristine Ca$_3$Ru$_2$O$_7$, where the Ru moments are ferromagnetically aligned within the metallic RuO$_2$ bilayers stacked in an antiferromagnetic fashion. The exceptionally shallow free energy landscape of this doped compound arises from intertwined electron-electron and electron-lattice interactions. This makes its magnetic and transport properties highly sensitive to external perturbations. We systematically investigated magnetic-field-induced phase switching in Ca$_3$(Ru$_{0.99}$Ti$_{0.01}$)$_2$O$_7$ to explore its magnetic $H$-$T$ phase diagram. With the field applied along the easy $b$-axis, parallel to the antiferromagnetic moments, the magnetization exhibits a first-order spin-flop transition at $\approx $ 6 T, indicating reorientation of the Ru moments perpendicular to the field. The transition is accompanied by a decrease in the electrical resistance, but the spin-flop phase remains insulating. Above 10.5 T, all Ru moments align with the $b$-axis, resulting in a forced ferromagnetic metallic phase. In contrast, neither spin-flop nor forced-ferromagnetic phases are observed up to 14 T, when the field is applied along the $a$-axis. While the electronic kinetic energy and the electron-lattice coupling contribute to the free-energy balance of this system, the resulting $H$-$T$ phase diagram is remarkably simple and closely resembles that of a canonical anisotropic antiferromagnet, albeit with substantially renormalized critical fields.
summary: The study investigates the field-induced phase diagram of $	ext{Ca}_3(	ext{Ru}_{0.99}	ext{Ti}_{0.01})_2	ext{O}_7$, an antiferromagnetic Mott insulator. By measuring magnetization and resistivity under applied fields, the authors reveal distinct first-order transitions along the easy axis, leading to a forced ferromagnetic metallic state. This work highlights the extreme sensitivity of correlated oxides to external perturbations.
main_problem: The study investigates magnetic field-driven phase switching in a bandwidth-controlled antiferromagnetic Mott insulator to map out its complex magnetic H-T phase diagram.
main_result: Applying a field along the easy $b$-axis induces a first-order spin-flop transition ($\approx 6$ T) followed by a forced ferromagnetic metallic state ($>10.5$ T), while the $a$-axis shows only conventional AFM suppression up to 14 T.
method: The research combines magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), magnetization ($M(H)$), and in-plane resistivity ($ho$) measurements under applied fields along different crystallographic axes.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Ca}_3(	ext{Ru}_{0.99}	ext{Ti}_{0.01})_2	ext{O}_7$, a Mott insulator derived from $	ext{Ca}_3	ext{Ru}_2	ext{O}_7$. Its properties are governed by intertwined electron-electron and electron-lattice interactions, leading to competing magnetic/metallic ground states.
key_observables: Magnetization ($M$), resistivity ($ho$), critical fields ($H_f^b$, $H_{	ext{sat}}^b$), and the temperature dependence of magnetic order ($T_N$).
important_parameters: Applied magnetic field strength (up to 14 T), doping concentration (1% Ti substitution), and temperature range (down to 5 K).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares experimental anomalies against theoretical models for anisotropic antiferromagnets, noting that the observed critical fields are significantly renormalized compared to simple Heisenberg models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\chi(T)$ vs $H$ and $M(H)$ vs $H$ along both axes. Color maps show $ho(T, H)$, detailing distinct phase boundaries corresponding to spin-flop and forced FM states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements of magnetic and transport properties as a function of applied field ($a$ vs $b$ axis) at low temperatures, building up the complete H-T phase diagram by correlating magnetization jumps with resistivity changes.
why_interesting: This work exemplifies how external fields can tune correlated electron systems between distinct insulating (Mott/AFM) and metallic (FM) phases, providing experimental realization of complex magnetic quantum phase transitions relevant to strongly correlated physics.
